title: Parsing the encoded first component
statement: Let $a,b,x$, and $p$ be bit strings, let $m\in\mathbb N$, and suppose $x=p\langle a,b\rangle$, where the encoding doubles every bit of $a$, appends $01$, and then appends $b$. Starting from state $0$ with the input head at position $|p|$, unary work tape content $1^m$, work head at $m$, and empty output, after $2|a|+2$ steps the extractor is in state $3$, with its input head at $|p|+2|a|+2$, work tape content $1^{m+|a|}$, work head at $m+|a|-1$, and empty output.
replaced: Let $a, b, p$ be bit strings, $x = p\,\langle a,b\rangle$ with $\langle a,b\rangle$ the self-delimiting pair encoding, and $m \in \mathbb{N}$. Then running $E$ for $2|a| + 2$ steps from $\Delta_x(0, |p|, m, m, \varepsilon)$ yields $\Delta_x(3, |p| + 2|a| + 2, m + |a|, m + |a| - 1, \varepsilon)$; here $E$ is the prefix-extraction machine (one work tape, states $\{0,1,2,3\}$) that counts the aligned data blocks $00$ and $11$ of a pair encoding $\langle a,b\rangle$ in unary on its work tape and then copies bits of $b$ to its output while moving its work head back along the counter, and $\Delta_x(q,i,m,h,o)$ denotes the configuration of $E$ on input $x$ in state $q$, with the input head on input position $i$ (counting from $0$), the work tape holding $1^m$ in cells $0,\dots,m-1$ and blanks elsewhere, the work head at $h$, and output $o$.
